a.text: The stargate's remodeling plan is an apparent success, and we have re-established a connection with Talos. A two-year backlog of information has been flooding in, but it is bare of any good tidings.
First it was the observatory stations on the asteroid belt, then the entire system's interstellar hub. Finally, the cruise fleets orbiting hospitable planets also fell into silence.
Even the ancient colonial fleet turned into a nomadic museum was not spared the same fate.
Along with these shocking revelations came similarly unexpected data left behind by Valeria. Her notes resembled her very being: long-winded and inexhaustible.

However, she seemed to have spent her last days repeatedly poring over literature and history alongside the technical documents. Studying how these great men died, what their last words and epitaphs were...
Like a child on the day before their coming-of-age ceremony, rifling through their parent's wardrobe in a frantic search for attire dignified enough for an adult.
Did she find her own life inadequate? Insufficiently weighty?
No, she left practically all that she had at the stargate. If she had lived in the past, wouldn't her achievements have been inserted into the annals of history?
But now it seemed nothing more than a narrow door opened between two tiny locked rooms in the dark. I fear it won't be long before the door is shut once more.
In the end, the history of humanity has exceeded the bounds of humanity itself, hah.

steps.name: 'Little Handy' from the Institute of Facility Management
steps.text: Reading error occurred (2).

steps.name: 'Little Handy' from the Institute of Facility Management
steps.text: Run fault diagnostics?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Do you need my help, Mr. Avitus?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Oh, no. I was merely observing this abandoned Little Handy.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Abandoned...? By who?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Don't worry, that's not important. What brings you here, Jordi?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm hoping to find something to do. We're clearly in dire straits, and I'm sure this city is full of problems in need of solving. They just won't reveal themselves to me.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Generally speaking, in that situation you should go to the Institute of Development Planning for an assessment.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: However, if you were looking for me specifically, I'll try my best to help you out.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You're a highly experienced and respected scholar, after all, and many in the city call you Magister.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Magister? My last work was 'The Death of Life,' a book with no educational value whatsoever.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-I read it, actually. Although I couldn't understand much, with so many cryptic words. Like starship, stargate... it seemed like from another world.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: 'Another world.' Hah, you're right about that.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: But I find myself undeserving of the title Magister. Often times I find myself lost in confusion.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Jordi, do you remember when I told you that blood ties were unimportant?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I do, but I already...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I may have been a bit misleading. While we indeed care little for blood relations, 'relationships' themselves are an excellent lead to follow.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: When one is lost, one ought to find a connection to reality—be it a life or an ideal—and seek a way out.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Otherwise you'll end up like me, sinking into an extended questioning of the value of your own existence.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: If I may be so bold, can I ask whatyour own 'relationship' is...?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: My Familiar.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: How, exactly...?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: She shared the same thoughts and goals, and would enrich both my spirit and my ideas. I loved her as ardently as I loved Ægir, as well as everything we've done for it.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I live a life surrounded by mountains of prehistoric material written in their strange script and incomprehensible grammar... I enjoy the process of translating it into Ægirian text.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: That was how we met, and I still remember how she'd throw herself into her work... Her eyebrows seemed to dance whenever she talked about something of interest to her.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: And when I told her so, in those exact words, she actually went to the Institute of Physical Art to find out if eyebrows could dance for real.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What a strange form of art... Did they manage it?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Strictly speaking, no. But some of their researchers were inspired to later develop the technology to make hair dance on its own.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: We've experienced the catastrophe that silenced the entire sea, and the Seaborn continue to threaten our existence, but we remain committed to exploring science, art, and our vision for the future.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Lava bridges that pump power from the planet's mantle, aquatic artery hubs that transform currents into fountains, artificial suns illuminating the depths of the oceanic abyss, and ecological bases filling the barren seafloor with life...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: We persist in transforming what the Predecessors lost into mystical megastructures. We need only a spark to spur on countless inventions.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: One hundred fifty years is truly too short.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: One hundred and fifty years?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Yes, the average lifespan of an Ægir.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: 'Short,' you say...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The more dangerous the era, the more valuable our creations become.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: We firmly believed in living fulfilling lives, and would gladly have gone to our end without regrets as we passed down the fire of civilization.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: We planned an educational system we believed was better than the Institute of Incubation.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Once our child was born via the incubator, we would raise them ourselves. They would possess a surging spirit and fresh ideologies, and become part of a more creative generation.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: It is unusual to raise children personally, but we had hoped to pass on the values we treasured from the fulfilling lives we'd lived.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So, what happened to her?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Dead.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Remember the Predecessor mentioned in 'The Death of Life'?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: He took shelter in an unknown refuge as he watched the sky pressing down on the earth every day. He already had a premonition of his own end.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: There was nothing he could do but calmly welcome its advent.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But that's someone else's life, a life far too distant from ours.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Is it, though? Are we not currently going through the same things?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Give it fifty years, maybe a hundred, and even the vast ocean may no longer hold a single drop of pure water.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The Seaborn have unwittingly overrun the ocean faster than we can create, devouring what we were once proud of, turning 'survival' into our only priority.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I watched as she was engulfed by despair. One day, she calmly gave up on our idea of raising our child ourselves.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: After all, everything we have inherited would only be lost in an era predestined to perish.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Five years ago, the Abyssal Hunters went to the lair of the Firstborn, and no one returned alive.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Soon after, she got sick, and died in depression. Our son was successfully born in the incubator, but I sent him to the Institute of Incubation.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: This was also when I began questioning the meaning of my own existence.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: My apologies, Jordi. I was supposed to be providing you guidance, wasn't I? I've already severed my relationship with the real world, but perhaps you have someone or something you still have ties with?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I gave up chasing Breogan long ago. I can't waste even more time chasing an unreachable shadow.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Maybe... Maybe I could delve into the notes he left, and learn how he developed his tech. And not just because I might be his descendant.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: ...But because you also have talent and dreams in that field.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: You can try the beacon tower, then. Breogan was involved in its reconstruction, so if you're familiar with his handiwork, perhaps you could help them out.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Every Ægir leaves their own quirks in their writings, theories, or technologies, so sometimes all you need to sort out a trickier part is someone more familiar with the author.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Thank you, Mr. Avitus!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Advisor Blandus? Are you alright?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The cultists failed to stop me from performing the surgery on the Hunters.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'm asking about your physical condition.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Thanks, Secunda. I see you're still—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Given your strange aversion to medical aid, someone has to confirm you're alright.

spans.text: Given your strange aversion to medical aid,

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Although judging from your condition, I'm guessing I'm not the first to try sending you to the hospital.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Perhaps the Waterway Program is too overwhelming. I'm something of a doctor myself, so I do know how to keep myself healthy—healthy enough to not slow down the program, anyway.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You know, you should take a look at the plant the cultists were using to kill people. It's difficult to imagine someone at the Institute of Ecological Art using it as paint.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Well, seeing how you're not in any immediate danger, I'll need you to cooperate with my investigation.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I saw Ulpianus. Recently.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I see you have too.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Only briefly, at the Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: And you didn't report this?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Catching a momentary glimpse of a familiar figure is hardly worth reporting.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'm not joking around, Advisor Blandus.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The data scientist's case has been confirmed to be a murder by the cultists, and it may be related to the assault on the lab.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Ulpianus seemed to know the victim well, and openly expressed his distrust of Ægir.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: He's always been like that. More action than words, and ever unwilling to reveal his reasons.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: His unique style doesn't explain all the doubts about him. I still need to check if he's linked to several Church cases.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: *sigh* Secunda, do you really lack any other leads or suspects more worthy of investigation?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Or I should ask, is this obsession with Ulpianus merely your own whim?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: *sigh*

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Secunda, I'm the one who rejected your application back then.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What did you just say?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I said, it was me who rejected your application to volunteer to become an Abyssal Hunter.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Ulpianus concurred, but I was the one who officially rejected you.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Why?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I saw your documents from the Institute of Development Planning. You'd written 'genetic research' in the box asking for your aspirations.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You only had to look at another file to see that becoming a Hunter was one another of my aspirations.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: We considered you extremely talented, even among the participants of the Abyssal Hunter project.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: During our technical discussions, you were the only one to ask Ulpianus ten questions in a row and get answers for all of them. The highest record for a freshman researcher.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The early transformation techniques were dangerous and unreliable. We were always searching for a better integration method. It was ultimately your theories that advanced the program's technology.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I considered it an honor back then, at least.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: But the program itself is nothing to be proud of, Secunda.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The concept was born nearly two centuries ago, a far cry from the average citizen's impression today. It was only twenty-some years ago that Ulpianus made it into a reality.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: In the hundred plus years before that, it was never afforded any systematic scrutiny or research. Only endless debates.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: To exploit our countrymen and integrate the flesh of other species into ourselves to save our humanity was tantamount to toppling the very foundations of Ægir.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: But Ulpianus is a decisive man. He can abandon his research, ideals, emotions, and even his humanity without a shred of hesitation. The sole principle he abides by is 'To benefit Ægir.'

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: And perhaps he will save Ægir someday, but our country should not be founded upon boundless self-sacrifice.

spans.text: save Ægir someday, but our country should not be founded upon boundless self-sacrifice.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Ulpianus understands better than anyone that his very existence is actually his country's woe.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: And so, 'The Abyssal Hunters do not need a second Ulpianus. Ægir should not have a second Ulpianus.'

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: 'There should be no one in Ægir who wishes to become another.'

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...I could practically hear him saying him.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I once joked to him how much better it would be if you were my student instead. Perhaps you could continue the research he and I used to work on: 'The evolution of Ægir cells.' Or perhaps you'd start a new field entirely.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You could have become one of the leading scientists of our time, with the opportunity to explore the primordial mysteries of all existence and lead us into the future.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Blandus, the two of you had no right.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'm sorry, Secunda.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Did you start reminiscing about the old days just to tell me I shouldn't bear a grudge against Ulpianus?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I did it so you'd see him in a new light.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Being too eager to capture him will do neither of you any good.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Aren't there cultists ready and available for questioning? Don't forget your duties, Secunda.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Where are they?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The first floor. In a booth in the equipment administration room. Do you need me to show you the way?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I know where it is. The Sea Patrol will take over the detainment of the criminals.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'm so sorry, but you can't go any further. We're currently—

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Wait, didn't I see you at the tribunal?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I know who you are, the emissary from land. If you don't mind me asking, what exactly are your duties on this diplomatic mission?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The data scientist seemed to have completely transformed into a Seaborn by the time she was found.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It would be difficult to obtain any further information from her, other than the fact that this set of data seems related to the 'Waterway' and the 'Beacons.'

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've finished analyzing the contents: there are unusual data interactions between the beacon within the city and the ones deployed in the nests.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The signals come from many spots within the city, and I have already inspected the port hub and any possible ships.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The only remaining location is Lab C-22. One of the earliest Abyssal Hunter experimental research labs.

options: You should be familiar with the place, then.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: However, it is far livelier here than I can remember it ever being.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Secunda has even deployed a garrison in the name of protecting Blandus.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A hindrance.

options: I'll help draw their attention if needed.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I can manage the Sea Patrol for now.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You should focus on the toughest target.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You would be... the Doctor of Rhodes Island, yes?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You say your institution helped diagnose and treat Oripathy in our Hunters, and now you hope to assist me with their organic regeneration surgery?

options: That's exactly what I'm here for.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Then you can leave with peace of mind.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The Church's assault here was just a minor episode, and the Hunters have already returned to their hibernation.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'll be constantly monitoring their physical condition, so your gaze—no matter how vigilant it may be—will be of little use in their recovery.

options: I see the Hunters were telling the truth.
You really have a terrible sense of humor.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...I see they have developed a deep friendship with you while wandering about on land.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Insist all you want, it doesn't change the fact that you will be of no help during the operation.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I mean no offense.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: This place was just recently raided, so please return to where you came from, for your own safety.
Blandus no longer pays you any attention, his gaze falling back onto the holographic projections before him.
Through those squares you can clearly see Gladiia, Skadi, and Laurentina deep asleep in a transparent gel.

You didn't manage to get a full grasp of Ægir's writing system before coming here. After days of fumbling your way through the city, you can still only recognize about half the symbols shown in the visuals.
But you observe a more important phenomenon within them:
Whenever Blandus selects an image, it would emit a faint beep.
That is to say, every chosen image generates a corresponding beep on the monitoring unit.

options: Could I help arrange the visual display?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I see you really want to stay. I won’t force you to leave, either. It seems you really do care for the Hunters, and I like people like you.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Little Handy, the Doctor is unfamiliar with the equipment in Ægir, so keep an eye on things.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Doctor, as long as you don't touch anything you shouldn't, then—

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The corridor's monitoring unit just beeped. Someone's looking in here.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Another beep for the experimental cabin in front and the corner further ahead... Hmm? There seems to be some sort of pattern.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Someone in the control room is rapidly switching the order of the holograms back and forth.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Doctor? What are you trying to tell me?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This way, then.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The operation is complete, Doctor. Thank you for your... fast and furious cooperation.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The Hunters will need another ten minutes to awaken, but I guarantee the procedure went without a hitch.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: So if you could now leave—

options: The Hunters seem to be deep asleep.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: They were unable to get any proper rest on land, despite what I'm sure was the best possible accommodation from you and Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Even now, they've just only arrived home, yet now must rush back to the frontlines.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: A single operation and hibernation session is far from enough to restore them to full strength.

options: It sounds like you tried your best.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I wouldn't say so, even if I've fulfilled my duties. There is a fundamental difference between the two, after all.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I believe you mentioned your expertise in the field of Oripathy?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Could you tell me what it's like, to be a patient?

options: They fight their fate for the rest of their lives.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: 'Fate'?

options: It means an inevitable direction or end.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Interesting. The ancient sages once discussed the concept of 'fate,' but it's been a long time since anyone has brought it up.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You see, Oripathy does not exist in the ocean, and most other diseases we managed to cure.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: We all choose our own paths in life, and the trajectory of our civilization is ours to define.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: For the longest time, we have forgotten what 'fate' even is.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Yet now, the ineradicable disease we've engraved into our Hunters' blood cannot be dealt with medically.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: To borrow your concept, one may call such an problem 'fate.'

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Each of the Hunters held their own dreams, their own lives. But now? They have no choice but to live alongside slaughter until they die themselves.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I've tried many methods to bring them back from this dead end, all to no avail.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Even now...

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: They seem to be in a hurry.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...I should get going too.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: It has been an honor to speak with you, Doctor. I hope you can take good care of them, if given the chance.
